clue.text: Cathedral city not backing Father Brown's progenitor

parts.note: Chester is an English cathedral city in Cheshire

indicators.note: backing means the little word beside it is read from right to left

explanation.surface: A cathedral city refuses to support the creator of a fictional priest-detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns 'not' into TON, which follows CHESTER. G. K. Chesterton wrote the Father Brown detective stories.
explanation.definitionFit: G. K. Chesterton was the author who invented the clerical sleuth Father Brown.

clue.text: Member of Egyptian sect caught by ear

indicators.note: by ear says we judge the word by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: caught, in slang, is copped, as when a thief is copped by police

explanation.surface: A member of an Egyptian religious group is captured by grabbing their ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by ear' is the homophone signal: COPPED (caught) said aloud sounds like COPT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Copts are Egypt's native Christian church, a religious community there.

clue.text: For example, Reginald, with paper debts, is shocking

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
Reg is the usual short form of the name Reginald
IOUs are written notes acknowledging money owed

explanation.surface: A man called Reginald running up written debts behaves scandalously.
explanation.walkthrough: IOU stands for 'I owe you', a signed slip promising repayment; plural IOUS ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something egregious is outstandingly bad, flagrant enough to appal.

clue.text: Italian maestro, knighted and noted for his "Goodbye"

definitions.text: Italian maestro, knighted and noted for his "Goodbye"

parts.words: Italian maestro, knighted and noted for his "Goodbye"
parts.note: a general-knowledge description of an Italian-born composer and singing teacher who was knighted in Britain and wrote the popular song Goodbye

explanation.walkthrough: Francesco Paolo Tosti, composer of the parlour song 'Goodbye' (1880), became Sir Paolo Tosti in 1908; the clue is a plain description with no wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Paolo Tosti was the Italian songwriter, knighted by Edward VII, best remembered for that farewell ballad.

clue.text: Again malice provides temporary relief

parts.note: the prefix re- means again, as in redo
spite is malice, a wish to hurt

explanation.surface: Renewed ill will, oddly, brings a short break from trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short pause or reprieve from something hard or unpleasant.

clue.text: Disputes about rebuilt pop-guns

indicators.note: rebuilt says the letters of the toy word are put together again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone argues over toy guns that have been reassembled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' rearranges the letters of POPGUNS; the hyphen is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppugn is a rare verb meaning to call into question or argue against.

clue.text: A medical officer's prophet

parts.note: MO is the abbreviation for medical officer, and the possessive 's adds an S

explanation.surface: An army doctor's personal seer.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive ending is used as a letter here: A + MO + S.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament, with a book named after him.

clue.text: Encountered about 39 384 inches

parts.note: to encounter someone is to have met them
re means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: A measurement taken of roughly a yard and a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed figure is garbled in the scanned text; a metre is about 39.37 inches.
explanation.definitionFit: The metric unit of length is a little over a yard, roughly thirty-nine inches.

clue.text: Dance of the Scottish valley

explanation.surface: A folk dance named after a Highland glen.
explanation.walkthrough: A strath is a broad Scottish river valley; Strathspey is the valley of the River Spey, which gave its name to a slow Scottish reel.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is a stately Scottish country dance; the second is the broad glen of the Spey in the Highlands.

clue.text: Leading medico in heavily wooded country

indicators.note: in says the doctor sits inside the woodland word

parts.note: a forest is land thick with trees
MO, medical officer, is a doctor or medico

explanation.surface: A top doctor is working out in the thick woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts MO inside FOREST.
explanation.definitionFit: Foremost means first in rank or position, at the front.

clue.text: Equality is capital in France

parts.note: par means equality, as in on a par

explanation.surface: A slogan about equality being the main thing in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Equality' calls up the French revolutionary motto, but it is only PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The French capital city is the seat of government on the Seine.

clue.text: Football fan involved in pure sport

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled or twisted together into a new order

explanation.surface: A football follower takes part in sport for its own sake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges PURE and SPORT together.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter is someone who follows and backs a team, a fan.

clue.text: Firing it between gin cock tails

indicators.note: between says the little word sits in the middle of the two mixtures
cocktails are mixed drinks, so gin is mixed up in each of the two

parts.note: taken as written, used twice for the two drinks

explanation.surface: Lighting up a match among the gin cocktails at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cock tails' is read as cocktails, mixtures of gin: two anagrams of GIN, IGN and ING, with IT 'between' them.
explanation.definitionFit: Igniting something is setting it on fire, as when a gun is fired by igniting the charge.

clue.text: Choose the chosen

explanation.surface: Pick out those already picked.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to pick by vote; as a noun the elect are those specially selected, as by God.

clue.text: In difficulties where the koala bears feed

explanation.surface: Struggling, as if stuck among the eucalyptus that koalas eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Koalas eat eucalyptus leaves, and eucalyptus trees are called gum trees; the idiom means in a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means stuck in trouble; literally it is high in a eucalyptus, where koalas browse.

clue.text: Paraffin gas reconstituted on paper

indicators.note: reconstituted means built up again in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fuel gas made again from paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconstituted' rearranges ON and PAPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Propane is a gaseous hydrocarbon of the alkane (paraffin) series, used as bottled fuel.

clue.text: A neat ham omelette is a detested object

indicators.note: an omelette is a jumble of beaten ingredients, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone loathes a tidy ham omelette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omelette' rearranges A NEAT HAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema is something or someone utterly loathed, originally a thing cursed by the church.

clue.text: Sporadic rain for demonstrators

explanation.surface: Light rain falling on protest marchers.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the word as 'show-ers', people who show or demonstrate something.
explanation.definitionFit: Showers are brief falls of rain; also people who exhibit or display things.

clue.text: How they lived happily in the fairy tale

definitions.text: How they lived happily in the fairy tale

parts.words: How they lived happily in the fairy tale
parts.note: a description of the stock closing line of a fairy story, where the couple live contentedly from then on

explanation.definitionFit: Fairy tales end 'and they lived happily' for the rest of time, the two words completing that formula.

clue.text: Postage adjusted by Nazi secret police

indicators.note: adjusted means altered or rearranged, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Stamp charges altered by Hitler's police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' rearranges POSTAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was the secret state police force of Nazi Germany.

clue.text: Aggression or transgression?

explanation.surface: Is it attacking or wrongdoing?
explanation.definitionFit: Offence is attack (as opposed to defence) and also a crime or misdeed.

clue.text: Peeping Tom on the high way?

definitions.text: Peeping Tom on the high way?

parts.words: Peeping Tom on the high way?
parts.note: a tom is a male cat, and its peeping organ set into a road would be a ..., the reflective stud on a highway

explanation.walkthrough: A Peeping Tom is a voyeur; here Tom is a tomcat, and 'high way' is the highway where reflective road studs are set. Cat's-eyes are road reflectors invented in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat's-eyes are glass reflectors set in road surfaces that shine in headlights.

clue.text: Terse affirmative turned up to make a bob

parts.note: curt means terse, rudely brief

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: yes is the affirmative reply

explanation.surface: A brief yes is reversed, earning someone a shilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses YES into SEY after CURT. 'bob' looks like the old shilling but is the bending of the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtsey is to bend the knees in a respectful dip, the bob women once made.

clue.text: Forward movement for the troops in Spring

explanation.surface: Soldiers advance as the seasons turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links the two senses; March is a spring month in the northern hemisphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers advance in step on a military walk; and the third month falls in spring.

clue.text: Additional clause could relate to equestrian

explanation.surface: An extra condition in a contract might concern horse riding.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an added provision to a document or bill; also someone on horseback.

clue.text: Clubman's warning to tolerate ancestor

parts.note: fore is the cry a golfer gives to warn people a ball is coming
to bear something is to tolerate it

explanation.surface: A golfer shouts a warning and puts up with an old relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubman' is a golfer, who shouts FORE before a stray shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is a forefather, someone from whom one is descended.

clue.text: Support second-class speed contest

parts.note: B is the grade below A, second class
a race is a contest of speed

explanation.surface: Backing a mediocre running event.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a strut or prop that supports something.

clue.text: Hail a small sloop-rigged vessel

parts.note: a hoy is a small coastal sailing boat, often rigged like a sloop

explanation.surface: Greeting a little sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A hoy is an old word for a small coasting vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahoy is the sailor's call used to hail another ship.

clue.text: True minds set first principles in disorder

indicators.note: set here means put or placed, as in set in a new arrangement
in disorder means jumbled up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sincere thinkers throw basic tenets into chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set ... in disorder' rearranges TRUE MINDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudiments are the basic elements of a subject, its starting points.

clue.text: Letter dropped at the start of a hand, for example

definitions.text: Letter dropped at the start of a hand, for example

parts.words: Letter dropped at the start of a hand, for example
parts.note: a description of the letter some speakers omit when they say 'and for hand

explanation.walkthrough: Dropping one's aitches is a mark of some regional British accents, saying 'and for hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is the spelt-out name of the eighth letter of the alphabet.

clue.text: Internal colour of the cruet

indicators.note: internal means within, so the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Describing the inside shade of a condiment holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Internal' picks the letters inside 'the cruet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is a pale greyish-yellow shade, like unbleached linen.

clue.text: Nervy start upsetting early finish? Not quite

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over and disturbing, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jittery opening throws off a premature ending, so it almost works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' and 'finish' place the pieces: the start is NERVY rearranged by 'upsetting', and EARLY comes at the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Very nearly means almost, falling just short.
